reading: November’s pre-dawn sky offers a diagonal configuration of four planets.
Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter will be observable without optical equipment in the eastern to south-eastern sky.
Of these four planets, Mercury will be the hardest to discern.
As the smallest planet and the one nearest the Sun, Mercury is persistently caught in solar glare.
Its visibility is confined to twilight, and it remains faint and low on the horizon.
An unobstructed south-eastern view across a flat horizon offers the recommended setting for spotting Mercury.
What makes Venus especially conspicuous is that only the Moon appears brighter in the night sky.
Among the major planets, Venus has the greatest reflectivity, the capacity to send incoming sunlight back into space.
Observers can distinguish Venus from nearby Spica by looking for a steady glow rather than the star’s twinkling.
Mars and Jupiter will be in particularly striking apparent proximity on 15 and 16 November.
According to astronomer Gideon Bendavid-Walker at the Royal Observatory Greenwich, their angular separation, the angle between their positions in the sky, will be just 1.2 degrees.
He compares that interval with the width of a finger held at arm’s length.
Near Regulus, the two planets may resemble a group of three stars.
While Uranus will be setting in the west before sunrise, Saturn and Neptune will be visible for a time in the evening.
Observers should choose a location away from artificial skyglow with a good view of the eastern horizon, allowing around twenty minutes for their eyes to acclimatise to darkness.
The recommended viewing period for the planetary parade is approximately 45–60 minutes before sunrise.

vocabulary.definition: The arrangement of several objects in relation to one another, considered as a whole.
To manage to see or recognise something that is difficult to distinguish from its surroundings.
Intense light from the Sun that makes nearby objects difficult to see.
Restricted to a particular situation, place or period; here, a limited lighting condition.
Having nothing in the way that blocks the view.
Readily noticeable because something stands out strongly from its surroundings.
The capacity of a surface to send incoming light back rather than absorb it.
Closeness as it appears to an observer, without establishing the actual distance between the objects.
The angle between the directions in which two objects are seen, rather than the distance between them in space.
To become accustomed to different surrounding conditions; here, for the eyes to become accustomed to darkness.

entries.ja: 複数の物体の互いの位置関係を、ひとまとまりとして捉えた配置。
entries.ko: 여러 물체가 서로 어떤 위치 관계에 있는지를 하나의 전체로 본 배치.
entries.zh-Hans: 将多个物体之间的相对位置作为一个整体来看时所呈现的排列方式。
entries.es: La disposición de varios objetos unos respecto de otros, considerada en su conjunto.
entries.pt-BR: A disposição de vários objetos uns em relação aos outros, considerada como um todo.
entries.fr: La disposition de plusieurs objets les uns par rapport aux autres, considérée dans son ensemble.
entries.de: Die Anordnung mehrerer Objekte im Verhältnis zueinander, als Ganzes betrachtet.

entries.ja: 周囲と見分けにくいものを、なんとか見たり、それが何かを認識したりすること。
entries.ko: 주변과 구별하기 어려운 것을 어렵게나마 보거나 알아보는 것.
entries.zh-Hans: 设法看见或认出难以与周围环境区分的事物。
entries.es: Lograr ver o reconocer algo que resulta difícil distinguir de su entorno.
entries.pt-BR: Conseguir ver ou reconhecer algo difícil de distinguir do que está ao redor.
entries.fr: Parvenir à voir ou à reconnaître quelque chose de difficile à distinguer de ce qui l’entoure.
entries.de: Etwas sehen oder erkennen können, das sich nur schwer von seiner Umgebung unterscheiden lässt.

entries.ja: 近くにある物体を見えにくくする、太陽からの強烈な光。
entries.ko: 가까이에 있는 물체를 보기 어렵게 만드는 태양의 강렬한 빛.
entries.zh-Hans: 使附近物体难以看清的强烈太阳光。
entries.es: Luz intensa del Sol que dificulta ver los objetos cercanos a él.
entries.pt-BR: Luz intensa do Sol que dificulta a visualização de objetos próximos a ele.
entries.fr: Lumière intense du Soleil qui rend les objets proches de lui difficiles à voir.
entries.de: Intensives Sonnenlicht, das Objekte in der Nähe der Sonne schwer erkennbar macht.

entries.ja: 特定の状況、場所、期間に限られていること。ここでは、特定の光の条件に限られていること。
entries.ko: 특정 상황, 장소 또는 기간에만 한정되는 것. 여기서는 특정한 빛의 조건에만 한정되는 것을 뜻한다.
entries.zh-Hans: 仅限于某种特定情况、地点或时段；这里指仅限于特定的光照条件。
entries.es: Limitado a una situación, un lugar o un período concreto; aquí, a unas condiciones de iluminación específicas.
entries.pt-BR: Restrito a uma situação, um lugar ou um período específico; aqui, a condições específicas de iluminação.
entries.fr: Limité à une situation, à un lieu ou à une période particulière ; ici, à des conditions d’éclairage bien précises.
entries.de: Auf eine bestimmte Situation, einen Ort oder einen Zeitraum beschränkt; hier auf bestimmte Lichtverhältnisse.

entries.ja: 視界を遮るものが何もないこと。
entries.ko: 시야를 가로막는 것이 전혀 없는 상태.
entries.zh-Hans: 没有任何东西挡住视线。
entries.es: Sin nada que se interponga y bloquee la vista.
entries.pt-BR: Sem nada no caminho que bloqueie a visão.
entries.fr: Sans rien qui fasse obstacle à la vue.
entries.de: Ohne etwas, das die Sicht versperrt.

entries.ja: 周囲から際立っているため、すぐに目につくこと。
entries.ko: 주변과 뚜렷하게 구별되어 쉽게 눈에 띄는 상태.
entries.zh-Hans: 因与周围环境形成鲜明区别而很容易被注意到。
entries.es: Fácil de notar porque destaca mucho de su entorno.
entries.pt-BR: Facilmente perceptível por se destacar bastante do que está ao redor.
entries.fr: Facile à remarquer parce qu’il se détache nettement de ce qui l’entoure.
entries.de: Leicht zu bemerken, weil es sich deutlich von seiner Umgebung abhebt.

entries.ja: 表面が、入ってくる光を吸収するのではなく、跳ね返す能力。
entries.ko: 표면이 들어오는 빛을 흡수하는 대신 되돌려 보내는 능력.
entries.zh-Hans: 表面将照射到的光反射回去而非吸收的能力。
entries.es: La capacidad de una superficie para devolver la luz que recibe en lugar de absorberla.
entries.pt-BR: A capacidade de uma superfície de devolver a luz que recebe, em vez de absorvê-la.
entries.fr: La capacité d’une surface à renvoyer la lumière qu’elle reçoit plutôt qu’à l’absorber.
entries.de: Die Fähigkeit einer Oberfläche, einfallendes Licht zurückzuwerfen, statt es aufzunehmen.

entries.ja: 物体間の実際の距離を示すものではなく、観察者から見たときの近さ。
entries.ko: 물체 사이의 실제 거리를 알려 주는 것은 아니며, 관찰자에게 보이는 가까운 정도.
entries.zh-Hans: 从观察者的角度看起来相近的程度，但这并不能确定物体之间的实际距离。
entries.es: La cercanía tal como la percibe un observador, sin que ello permita establecer la distancia real entre los objetos.
entries.pt-BR: A proximidade tal como aparece para um observador, sem que isso estabeleça a distância real entre os objetos.
entries.fr: La proximité telle qu’elle apparaît à un observateur, sans que cela permette d’établir la distance réelle entre les objets.
entries.de: Die Nähe, wie sie einem Beobachter erscheint, ohne damit den tatsächlichen Abstand zwischen den Objekten festzustellen.

entries.ja: 空間内での二つの物体の距離ではなく、それぞれが見える方向の間の角度。
entries.ko: 두 물체 사이의 실제 공간상 거리가 아니라, 각 물체가 보이는 방향 사이의 각도.
entries.zh-Hans: 观看两个物体时，视线方向之间形成的夹角，而不是它们在空间中的距离。
entries.es: El ángulo entre las direcciones en las que se ven dos objetos, en lugar de la distancia que los separa en el espacio.
entries.pt-BR: O ângulo entre as direções em que dois objetos são vistos, em vez da distância entre eles no espaço.
entries.fr: L’angle entre les directions dans lesquelles on voit deux objets, plutôt que la distance qui les sépare dans l’espace.
entries.de: Der Winkel zwischen den Richtungen, in denen zwei Objekte zu sehen sind, und nicht ihr Abstand im Raum.

entries.ja: 異なる周囲の環境に慣れること。ここでは、目が暗さに慣れること。
entries.ko: 달라진 주변 환경에 익숙해지는 것. 여기서는 눈이 어둠에 익숙해지는 것을 뜻한다.
entries.zh-Hans: 逐渐适应不同的周围环境；这里指眼睛逐渐适应黑暗。
entries.es: Acostumbrarse a condiciones distintas del entorno; aquí, que los ojos se acostumbren a la oscuridad.
entries.pt-BR: Acostumar-se a condições diferentes do ambiente; aqui, os olhos se acostumarem à escuridão.
entries.fr: S’habituer à des conditions ambiantes différentes ; ici, pour les yeux, s’habituer à l’obscurité.
entries.de: Sich an andere Umgebungsbedingungen gewöhnen; hier, dass sich die Augen an die Dunkelheit gewöhnen.

review.method: separate ChatGPT plan translation and independent editing sessions
